question: An analyst had 174 data points. She divided by 2 for two analysis groups. She multiplied by 8 for detailed breakdown. She multiplied by 3 for cross-verification. She added 60 from additional samples (measured in verified data points). Throughout analysis, morning data collection, afternoon processing, and evening verification tracked progress, with one quantity tracked through its final state. What was the verified data point count?

A store manager began with 60 items. They subtracted 52 from morning sales. They added 27 from restocking. They subtracted 14 from damage. They subtracted 3 more from shrinkage (measured in final inventory items). Throughout the day, morning opening, afternoon customers, and evening closeout tracked movement. What was the final inventory count?

A retailer had 225 inventory units. He multiplied by 2 through restocking. He multiplied by 5 for warehouse expansion. He added 38 new items. He multiplied by 4 for display calculation. He multiplied by 9 for annual projection (measured in annual inventory units). Throughout the year, morning receiving, afternoon stocking, and evening audits tracked growth. What was the annual inventory projection?

A project manager had 164 hours. He multiplied by 4 for team allocation. He divided by 4 for realistic capacity. He subtracted 91 from committed work. He subtracted 26 from other priorities (measured in available project hours). Throughout the period, morning planning, afternoon tasks, and evening review structured one time-ordered journey. What was the available project hour total?

A manager oversaw 130 tasks. She subtracted 59 for completed items. She added 29 from new assignments. She multiplied by 6 for team scaling. She subtracted 204 for delegation. She divided by 4 for fair distribution. She added 52 from contingency (measured in distributed task units). Michael compared workload with his team. What was the distributed task unit count?

A project started with 231 items. She subtracted 194 for phase completion. She added 72 from new scope. She subtracted 15 for scope reduction. She multiplied by 6 for team deliverables (measured in team deliverable units). Throughout the project, morning planning, afternoon execution, and evening review tracked time-ordered stages. What was the team deliverable unit count?

A facility had 93 resources. He multiplied by 6 for usage factor. He multiplied by 9 for daily demand. He multiplied by 5 for demand scaling. He multiplied by 5 for peak capacity. He subtracted 108086 for major allocation. He subtracted 3653 from final adjustment (converting to adjusted resource capacity, measured in dollars from cents). What was the adjusted resource capacity?

A company generated 223 revenue units. They multiplied by 5 for quarterly expansion. They multiplied by 2 for regional multiplication. They multiplied by 7 for country-wide scaling. They added 55 from special initiatives (measured in annual revenue units). Converting through morning operations, afternoon sales, and evening planning. What was the annual revenue unit total?

A team began with 151 work hours. They subtracted 131 for completed tasks. They subtracted 6 for administrative time. They multiplied by 8 for output calculation. They multiplied by 4 for daily scaling. They multiplied by 6 for weekly projection (measured in weekly work units). Throughout the week, morning standups, afternoon work, and evening reviews tracked progress. What was the weekly work unit projection?

Sarah began the month with 217 dollars. She earned 46 dollars from tutoring. She then spent 143 dollars on supplies. Later she found 19 dollars. Finally she earned 28 dollars from freelance work. Her brother had 600 dollars but that's not relevant. How much money does Sarah have now?

Elena started with 179 apples. She gave away 177 apples to neighbors, keeping only 2. Then she bought 29 apples at the market. She picked 6 more from her tree. She used 35 apples for pie. She harvested 43 more apples. (The garden shed held a dozen storage boxes, but that's not part of her count.) Finally, she gave away 21 apples. How many apples does Elena have?

A farmer started with 143 chickens. He added 43 more to his flock. Each chicken laid 8 eggs per week, giving him 8 times his chicken count in eggs. He then sold 864 eggs at market. The remaining eggs were split evenly into 2 packs for sharing. How many eggs did the farmer have after splitting them?

Tom had 164 stickers. He multiplied his collection by buying 4 packs. Each pack had more than he expected, so he added 26 stickers. He then created 8 sets with these stickers. Each set was duplicated 7 times through copying. He added 29 more stickers at the end. His friend's collection was separate from his totals. How many stickers does Tom have?

A store began with 227 boxes of cereal. They received 19 more boxes. They then arranged them in 9 rows, multiplying the total by 9. They removed 957 boxes to donation centers. They then removed 217 more boxes as defective. Each remaining box was packaged in groups of 5. The warehouse manager had 100 boxes elsewhere. How many groups of 5 did they end up with?

A grocery store had 215 cans. They added 60 cans to inventory. They arranged displays with 7 times as many cans. They removed 1734 cans for sale. They restocked 122 more cans later. They donated 68 cans to a food bank. Each can was marked at cents per unit (prices separate from count). How many cans remain?

A toy store had 29 toys. They added 23 toys. They received 28 more toys. They then had to donate 50 toys. The remaining toys were packed into sets of 5 toys each. How many toys did they have in total after packing?

A baker started with 89 bags of flour. She multiplied by making 7 batches, then multiplied by 7 again. She added 60 more bags. She used 1502 bags for products. She gained 74 bags from a supplier. His friend had 200 bags elsewhere. Converting from minutes to hours, she worked through both morning and afternoon to evening. How many bags does she have?

A library had 214 books on Monday. They removed 158 books for repair. They removed 47 more books from circulation. They removed 5 additional damaged books. The remaining books were divided into 4 separate reading groups. They gained 55 books as donations in dollars per volume (units separate). How many books per group?

Maria earned 205 dollars. She added 35 dollars from a bonus. She received 13 dollars from tips. She gained 29 dollars from interest. She then quadrupled her earnings for a calculation. She spent 1351 dollars on a purchase. Morning income, afternoon deposits, and evening accounting confirmed the total. The minutes she worked converted to hours. How much money does Maria have now?

David had 134 video games. He multiplied by 7 for a collection estimate. He removed 347 games (selling some). He gained 5 games as gifts. He removed 514 games for donation. He added 56 games. Morning gaming session, afternoon organizing, evening inventory check. His friend had 200 games. How many games does David have?

Ryan started with 86 points. He earned 6 points. He lost 90 points in a penalty. He then multiplied by 8 times due to a bonus round. He lost 5 points. He gained 69 points from winning. He multiplied again by 8 times for final scoring. His teammate had double his points. Someone else had 400 points but that's not tracked here. How many points does Ryan have at the end?

A factory started with 78 widgets. They produced 4 batches, then 8 more batches, then 8 more batches, then doubled the output once more. They added 3 bonus widgets. Tom's factory had fewer widgets. How many widgets were produced?

A restaurant had 172 plates. They added 41 plates. They removed 174 plates for washing. They divided remaining by 3 sections. They removed 6 plates (broken). They added 41 plates (new). They added 42 plates (cleaned). Each convert from minutes to hours took time. Morning prep, afternoon service, evening cleanup. Jake had fewer plates. How many total plates?

A school library had 88 books. They removed 17 books for repair. They then doubled the remaining (twice the amount). They added 57 more books. They added 63 more books. They tripled the collection. The morning's inventory versus evening's count showed growth. Someone had half as many books. How many books total?

A farmer had 138 dollars. He spent 7 dollars. He removed 111 dollars more. He added 32 dollars. He then multiplied by 6 times for a loan calculation. Converting from cents to dollars helped with accounting. How much money does he have?
